changes.before: A prism has an equilateral-triangle cross-section. A ray enters and leaves through adjacent faces at equal distances from their common refracting apex. The prism material has index $n>0$. The same external medium on both faces has index $n_a>0$, which is not fixed at $1$. Count only nongrazing rays that actually enter, cross and leave the prism. Which statement gives the allowable range and supremum (least upper bound) for any $n_a>0$, and correctly states whether a greatest allowable value exists?
changes.after: A prism has an equilateral-triangle cross-section. A ray enters and leaves through adjacent faces at equal distances from their common refracting apex. Consider only direct single-pass transmission between these two faces: inside the prism, the ray follows one straight segment joining its entry and exit points, without internal reflection.
